The issue was first reported by Marcus Reeves (mreeves@corplabs.com) from the Atlanta integration engineering team and affected the Integration Gateway path used by the nightly data synchronization process. Approximately 1,400 records queued for sync to the downstream CRM pipeline were blocked.

The alert was initially raised by Priya Nair via the #api-incidents Slack channel. Missing initial context included token expiry state and whether the downstream service was slow or rate limiting during the failure window.

title: Internal DNS names failing to resolve from corporate resolver
description: Internal users and dependent services across the Denver office were trying to resolve hostnames under corp.local through the corporate DNS resolver (dns-resolver-01.corp.local, 10.20.1.10), but lookups intermittently returned NXDOMAIN, SERVFAIL, or outdated A records instead of the current internal addresses. The issue was first reported by Marcus Ellison (EMP-40821) from the infrastructure team, who noticed that internal-portal.corp.local, service-discovery.corp.local, and inventory-api.corp.local were unreachable by name from his workstation WORKSTATION-DELL-ME (10.20.44.87). Monitoring indicated the authoritative internal DNS servers (ns1-auth.corp.local, ns2-auth.corp.local) had updated records while the corporate resolver continued serving stale cached responses from corp-dc-1. Several other users including Priya Nagarajan also confirmed intermittent failures from their machines.

title: Intermittent NXDOMAIN for internal host 'app-db.internal' from one client subnet

title: Internal hostname fails to resolve — stale A record in internal DNS
description: Multiple internal users and monitoring agents were trying to reach app.example.internal, but name resolution intermittently returned NXDOMAIN or the outdated IP address 10.20.5.47 from internal DNS. The issue was first reported by Priya Nambiar (emp ID E-40291) from the Austin office, who noticed the internal-app-service dashboard was unreachable by hostname. Additional reports came in from the Portland development team. The application could not connect to its backend by hostname, impacting internal app access across datacenter-1. Investigation focused on the internal BIND 9 zone data on dns-primary-01.dc1.internal and resolver cache behavior after a stale A record remained in the zone for a decommissioned address (10.20.5.47) instead of the current backend at 10.20.8.112.

title: Internal hostname svc-db.internal fails DNS resolution
description: Internal application teams were trying to reach the database service by the internal hostname svc-db.internal, but several application pods intermittently failed name resolution and could not connect to the DB. The issue was first reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado@corplabs.com) from the platform engineering group in Phoenix. Failures were concentrated on queries served by dns-resolver-01.corp.internal, where monitoring showed repeated NXDOMAIN responses from client hosts including WORKSTATION-LINUX-MD (10.42.17.88). Review of the internal DNS zone found an outdated A record pointing to decommissioned IP 10.20.5.14 instead of the current 10.20.9.42, along with a deprecated zone management policy reference (internal-dns-policy-v1), creating impact for internal-order-service, payment-processor, and reporting-worker in corp-datacenter-1.

Impact was cross-site and intermittent, affecting access to internal endpoints and application connectivity. Initial report came in via Slack from mdelgado@corplabs.com.

The issue impacted name-based access to the internal database endpoint across multiple subnets (10.22.4.0/24 and 10.22.6.0/24) in the on-premises us-east-1 datacenter. Additional reports came in from Priya Nair (pnair@corplabs.com) on the observability team, confirming the same symptoms from hosts in Rack 14B.

title: Internal host failing to resolve
description: Engineering users in the Arlington office were trying to reach internal-app.company.local on the internal network, but between 09:12 and 09:40 EST the hostname intermittently failed to resolve and client systems received NXDOMAIN responses. The issue was first reported by Marcus Delgado (mdelgado, EMP-40821) via the #dns-ops Slack channel and affected access to the internal application by name through the BIND 9 cache cluster (cache-east-01.infra.company.local / cache-east-02.infra.company.local) in the us-east-1 primary datacenter. Investigation tied the failures to an outdated internal DNS A record pointing to the decommissioned IP 10.22.4.17 instead of the current 10.22.8.55, and delayed remediation because the runbook referenced a deprecated DNS change-control policy (POL-DNS-2019, superseded by POL-DNS-2025).
